 Orders On Main Petition
 1. This is petition filed by the petitioner u/sec. 12 of
Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act,
2005.
 2. By filing this petition the petitioner has sought
 3
 C.Misc. 98/2018
various reliefs fallen U/sec. 18, 19, 20 and 22 of Pwdv
Act-2005.
 3. The format as required under the Dv Act is duly
filled up and the same is presented by the petitioner
along with the affidavit. In the required format, the
detail of the petitioners' case cannot be made out, the
same can be gone through in the evidence let in by the
petitioner. Hence, before considering the reliefs sought
for, it becomes just and necessary to look into the case
of the petitioner. 
 4. The petitioner stated that she is legally wedded
wife of the respondent no.1. The marriage was arranged
marriage which took place on 11.10.2012 at St.Misba
Church, Magadi Road. The said marriage was
performed as per Christian mythology rites and
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024 
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
2

customs in presence of the elder's of both the family
members and registered the same before the above said
 4
 C.Misc. 98/2018
church. At the time of the marriage, the petitioner's
parents have given the dowry Rs.25,000/- and gold
ornaments gold chain, golden finger ring total 12 grms
towards dowry and also the petitioner's parents have
spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for marriage expenses
as per the direction of 1st respondent and his parents. 
The petitioner submits that, after the marriage both the
petitioner and respondent lived together in matrimonial
house as shown in the cause title address. The
petitioner further submits that out of the wedlock,
there are no issues. 
 5. The petitioner further submits that the mother of
the respondent no.1 used to harass the and picked up
quarrel with the petitioner without any reason or cause. 
The mother of the 1st respondent who is the 2nd
respondent used to say that the petitioner has to bring
home more dowry from the petitioner's parents and she
 5
 C.Misc. 98/2018
has not allowed the petitioner to live in the matrimonial
house. The petitioner submits that however the 1st
respondent has assaulted the petitioner mercilessly and
at that time she has given complaint before the
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
3

Mahalakshmi Layout police station against the 1 st 
respondent. 
 6. The petitioner further submits that after she
became eight months pregnancy, the pregnancy was
terminated and child died in the year 2013, the
respondents have not given proper food to the
petitioner and always demanded dowry and
respondents used to sent the petitioner for coolie work
and they were not giving rest to the petitioner and the
1st respondent has not shown any love and affection
towards the petitioner. Due to said reasons, since 2013
to 2017, 4 to 5 times, the petitioner had to under gone
abortion and she was forced to work like machine. The
 6
 C.Misc. 98/2018 
1st respondent and his parents have not spent any
single rupee to the petitioner's welfare and always he
used to say lie and he is suspicious mind of person.
 7. The petitioner submits that she is working as
house servant and the entire her earnings and some of
her gold ornaments have kept with the pan broker's
shop and the petitioner has paid chit money for
clearing the house loan. Therefore, the petitioner is
unable to live with the respondents from August 2017. 
As the 1st respondent has totally failed and neglected to
maintain her in all manners. Therefore, left with no
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
4

option, she started to live with her parent's house
which is an shown in the cause title address. The
petitioner submits that, the 1st respondent has been
working as Welder at Micro Company private ltd., at
Peenya 2nd stage, Bengaluru and he is getting monthly
salary of Rs.25,000/- and the 1st respondent is having
 7
 C.Misc. 98/2018
own house. Therefore, it is essential to lead her life and
now a days very difficulty to lead her day to day life. 
Hence, this petition for domestic violence. 
 8. On service of notice, the respondents have
appeared before court and filed vakalath through his
counsel. The respondent no.1 submits that the
respondent nos.2 to 4 are his mother and siblings. The
petitioner has unnecessarily involved them in the
petition just to harass the respondents and there is no
alleged role of the respondents in the allegations by the
petitioner in the entire petition . Further, the
respondent no.2 is a aged women suffering from
multiple ailments and the respondent no.3 is married
and living separately in her matrimonial home as such
she has no role, interest or involvement in the
matrimonial home. After the marriage the petitioner
demanded for a separate residence with the respondent
 8
 C.Misc. 98/2018
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024 
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
5

no.1 as the respondent no.1 was residing with his
mother and brother and the house was old one. 
Accordingly, the respondent no.1 rented a house at
Someshwaranagar, near Mahalakshmi Layout,
Bengaluru and lived there for nearly 2 yrs. Thereafter,
the respondent no.1 along with the petitioner got
shifted to another rented accommodation near 2 nd
cross, Ashokpuram, Bengaluru. 
 9. The petitioner often used leave home stating that
she was visiting her parental home, but when inquired
the respondent no.1 came to know that, the petitioner
never visited her parental home and when the
respondent no.1 questioned about the same the
petitioner started to quarrel and on the said day the
petitioner's brother along his others assaulted the
respondent no.1 and filed a police complaint against
him without his fault. 
 9 
 C.Misc. 98/2018 
 10. The respondent no.1 has spent all his earnings
towards the petitioner's medical expenditure and the
respondent no.2 used to cook food for the petitioner
even though she being old aged and having multiple
aliments as the petitioner would never take interest in
the house hold activities in the guise of work and
health issues. The respondent no.1 was earlier working
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
6 

as Welder at Micro company private Ltd., but
unfortunately has lost the job due to nation-wide
lockdown and is currently working as a random daily
wager like painter an labourer etc. The respondent no.1
during the petitioner's whole period of stay in the
matrimonial home has fulfilled his marital obligations
and has maintained the petitioner to best of his
capabilities. The petitioner is currently running a
clothing store and has sufficient means and source of
income to maintain her and she is residing with her
 10
 C.Misc. 98/2018
parents. The avernments made in the present petition
filed by the petitioner does not constitute any domestic
violence, hence the present petition filed under this act
is not maintainable and the same is liable to be
dismissed. 
 11. Keeping in mind the evidence given by the
petitioner it becomes just and necessary to look into
whether the orders required by the petitioner various
reliefs which are fallen U/Sec. 18, 19, 20 & 22 of Dv
Act can be granted. 
 12. The petitioner in support of her case has got
examined herself as Pw.1 and got exhibited documents
as Exs.P.1 & 2. Ex.P.1 is marriage certificate, Ex.P.2 is
adhar card. 
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/ 
7 

 13. The counsel for the petitioner filed written
arguments and perused the materials placed on record. 
 11 
 C.Misc. 98/2018
 14. The points that arise for consideration are:-
 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled
 for protection order relief as
 contemplated U/sec.18 of Dv Act?
 2.Whether the petitioner is entitled
 for residence relief as contemplated
 U/sec.19 of Dv Act?
 3. Whether the petitioner is entitled
 for monetary relief as contemplated
 U/sec. 20 of Dv Act? 
 4.Whether the petitioner is entitled
 for compensation relief as
 contemplated U/sec. 22 of Dv Act? 
 5. What order? 
 15. The findings to the above points are as
 follows:-
 Point Nos.1 to 4 - In the Negative
 Point No.5 - As per Final Order, for the
 following:-
 Reasons
 16. Reasoning on Point Nos.1 to 4: Since these
points are interconnected with each other and requires
 12
 C.Misc. 98/2018
common appreciation of evidence, hence to avoid
repetition of facts all the points are taken together for
common consideration. 
 17. The case of the petitioner is that the
respondents have given mental and physical
harassment and for grant of permanent
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
8

accommodation. The petitioner has sought for various
reliefs which are fallen U/sec. 18, 19, 20 and 22 of Dv
Act.
 18. In the affidavit filed by the petitioner along with
petition she has stated that the averments made in the
petition are all true and correct. The petitioner has
stated that she was subjected to verbal and emotional
abuse and she was also subjected to economic violence
by not providing money for maintaining herself. 
Further, the petitioner stated that the respondent no.1
and his mother always tortured the petitioner both
 13
 C.Misc. 98/2018
mentally and physically by abusing her in filthy
language without any reason. The respondent no.1
being husband of the petitioner did not control the
illegal acts of the mother-in-law. Thereafter, the
respondents have neglected the petitioner and also
avoiding maintaining the petitioner for one or other
reasons. When the petitioner tried to leave her marital
house, the respondent was not living the petitioner to
lead her own life. But, in the objections, the
respondents have denied all allegations made by the
petitioner. Further, the respondents stated that the
petitioner herself has neglected the respondent no.1
and his mother by abusing them. Thereafter she left the
matrimonial home without any reason and staying with
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
9

her parents.
 19. It is submitted that soon after the marriage the
petitioner came to the matrimonial home to cohabit
 14
 C.Misc. 98/2018
with the respondents. During the stay of petitioner in
the matrimonial home , the respondent no.1 has
fulfilled his marital obligations towards the petitioner.
Without any reason the petitioner has filed this
petition.
 20. Further on perusal of the petition, it can be
seen that the petitioner and respondent no.1 are living
in shared household, at that time the respondent and
her mother have harassed the petitioner emotionally
and mentally by not taking care of her. On the other
hand, the respondents have also filed objections by
denying the allegations of the petitioner leveled against
them. Thereafter, also the respondent had looked after
the petitioner with fulfilling her all necessities with love
and affection. 
 21. No doubt, as per Sec.3 of Dv Act, if at all the
respondent commits any domestic violence as above
 15
 C.Misc. 98/2018
pleaded is fully established by the petitioner then
definitely the petitioner will be entitled for an order of
residential orders as per Sec.19 of Dv Act and
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
10

mandatory reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20 of the
Act.
 22. As per Sec.19 of Dv Act while disposing an
application U/sec.12(1) Pwdv Act, a Magistrate, may
on being satisfied that the domestic violence has taken
place can pass residence order restraining the
respondent from dispossessing or in any other manner
disturbing the possession of the petitioner from the
shared household . 
 23. In the case on hand, it is the case of the
petitioner that she is residing along with the
respondents after the marriage in the shared house. 
When in the respondents have given mental and
emotional torture and also he neglected the petitioner. 
 16
 C.Misc. 98/2018 
 24. On perusal of the pleadings as well as evidence
of both sides, it appears that there is no such domestic
violence caused by the respondents against the
petitioner. Further, it appears that the petitioner herself
has left the matrimonial home and went to her parents
house without giving any intimation to the respondent. 
Therefore, the question of granting residential orders as
per Sec.19 of Dv Act cannot be considered in favour of
the petitioner. 
 25. With regard to the possession of mandatory
reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20, it becomes just
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
11

and necessary for the petitioner to establish the same. 
 26. The fact that both petitioner and the
respondent no.1 are wife and husband is not in
dispute. When the petitioner has let in evidence she
has stated that subsequent to marriage, she is residing
along with the respondents in the shared household, in
 17
 C.Misc. 98/2018
their the respondents have intentionally neglected the
petitioner. The said contention had been categorically
denied by the respondents. Further, he stated that
without any reason the petitioner has left the
matrimonial home. At this stage, no need to act like
what the petitioner stated in her petition. 
 27 . On the other hand, after service of notice, the
respondents have appeared before the court by filing
vakalath from their counsel and filed objections to the
main petition by denying all averments pleaded by the
petitioner in her petition. 
 28 The petitioner examined herself as Pw-1 by
filing affidavit of examination-in-chief. In the said
examination-in-chief, she reiterated the averments of
the petition. But, the counsel for the respondent has
not cross examined the Pw.1. Therefore, the cross of
Pw.1 is taken as nil. Further, the respondent has not
 18
 C.Misc. 98/2018
lead his evidence. Then the evidence of respondent is
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
12

taken as nil. In the evidence, the Pw.1 marked only two
documents on her behalf i.e., marriage certificate and
copy of adhar card. Except these documents and
allegations made by her in the petition, the petitioner
has not furnished any documents to show that the
respondent have caused domestic violence against her. 
It seems that there was no any domestic violence
caused by the respondents towards the petitioner. 
 29. On going through the oral and documentary
evidence as well as affidavit of assets liabilities
furnished by both parties, it is clear that the petitioner
is not having any source income. On the other hand,
the respondent no.1 is working as Welder at Micro
Company private Ltd., at Peenya 2nd stage, Bengaluru
and he is getting monthly salary of Rs.50,000/- and the
1st respondent is having own house. Even though,
 19
 C.Misc. 98/2018
looking into the oral and documentary evidence of the
petitioner, it clear that there is no any domestic
violence caused by the respondent towards the
petitioner. Further, she is utterly fails to prove her case
by oral and documentary evidence. 
 30. On perusal of the entire pleadings and
documents and oral testimony of the petitioner, it is
crystal clear that the petitioner is legally wedded wife of
respondent no.1 and both are living in the shared
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
13

house under same roof. Further, it is clear that the
respondents have not given any harassment mentally
and physically to the petitioner.
 31. It is undisputed that on the date of filing the
petitioner was legal wedded wife of respondent no.1. 
When the petitioner is herself failed to prove her case, it
has to be considered as the respondent no.1 has not
caused any domestic violence against the petitioner as
 20
 C.Misc. 98/2018
alleged by the petitioner in her petition. 
 32 . Further, the petitioner is failed to prove the
allegations which are made by her in the petition as
well as in examination in chief in respect of domestic
violence caused by the respondent u/sec. 3 of Pwdv
Act.
 The Section 3 in The Protection of Women from
Domestic Violence Act, 2005 reads as under;
Sec. 3. Definition of domestic violence.--
 For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or
 commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute
 domestic violence in case it. 
 (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life,
 limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the
 aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing
 physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse
 and economic abuse; or
 (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved
 person with a view to coerce her or any other person
 related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry
 or other property or valuable security; or
 (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or
Sharada vs R Vadivelu Alias Samuel And Others on 13 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102043342/
14

 any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in
 clause (a) or clause (b); or
 (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or
 21
 C.Misc. 98/2018
 mental, to the aggrieved person.
 33. On careful perusal of the above section, it is
clear that in this case, the respondents have not
committed any domestic violence against the petitioner
as explained above. On discussing above, if the
respondents have not committed any domestic violence
against the petitioner, as contemplated u/sec. 3 of
Pwdv Act, the petitioner is not entitled for any of the
reliefs as prayed by her in the petition. Hence, this
court answer these point nos.1 to 4 in the the negative. 
 34. Point No.5: In view of the findings on the
above point nos.1 to 4 and the reasons stated therein,
this court proceed to pass the following: -
 Order
The petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence
Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed.

(Kusuma. V) JMFC (TC-III), Bengaluru.
